"We thank our partners for all this support," Zelensky posted on Telegram on Tuesday. Speaking at a press conference with Estonian President Alar Karis, he said Ukraine needed more of the interceptor missiles. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Zelensky has for weeks criticized Western allies for failing to honour delivery pledges, saying they preferred to keep the weapons for themselves. On Sunday, Zelensky said Ukraine urgently needed 300 Patriot missiles as part of a winter package, while the country's air force had put its requirement at 360. He told Ukrainian media at a weekend meeting that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz had committed to delivering a total of 600 missiles between 2027 and 2028. The Patriot air-defence system is considered particularly effective against Russia's fast ballistic missiles, and Moscow has recently exploited gaps in Ukraine's defences to carry out a particularly high number of missile strikes. Zelensky said at the weekend that Russia was capable of producing up to 1,300 ballistic missiles a year. "At present they have between 600 and 630," he said. "We have a rough idea of the number they want to reach between now and the end of winter. At a rough estimate, they could produce 100 ballistic missiles a month." Photograph: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/AP Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Poland’s Tusk heads to Kyiv after warning of Russian strikes on Ukrainian allies Donald Tusk says Moscow will not enter peace talks without Ukraine’s ‘total capitulation’ and will try to inflict a ‘tragically critical’ winter. What we know on day 1,668 Warren Murray and agencies Thu 17 Sep 2026 21.47 EDT Last modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 21.49 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Russia is planning hybrid strikes with drones or rockets on European countries supporting Ukraine , among them Poland according to its prime minister, Donald Tusk. Russia will pretend the attacks are “accidental” in order to “paralyse or at least weaken the motivation of Nato countries” to rush to the defence of the member state coming under attack, Tusk said in a speech to the Polish parliament. “There is a real risk that drones or other types of projectiles will enter the territory of one or several countries on the eastern flank and even cause destruction,” Tusk said, vowing that “if anyone dares to attack us, they will face a resolute response from us and our allies” . Tusk announced he would travel to Ukraine overnight, arriving on Friday, in what might be seen as an act of defiance against Russia after European leaders were in transit during a drone strike on a train near the Polish-Ukrainian border on Sunday. Officials usually keep their travel plans to Ukraine secret for security reasons. In Kyiv, he said he would discuss with Volodymyr Zelenskyy how to defend against the new types of drones, as well as discuss with partners including Slovakia further sanctions against Russia. The Slovak ⁠prime minister, Robert ​Fico, ‌also said ‌he would be in Kyiv as he claimed Europe is closer ⁠than ever to a large-scale ⁠war erupting ⁠from ​the war in Ukraine ⁠and politicians must strive for peace. Fico has ‌kept warm relations with Russia while criticising EU and Nato aid to Ukraine, though Slovakia’s arms industry is simultaneously a producer of artillery shells supplied to Kyiv’s forces. On Friday ⁠the European Union will ⁠disburse €3.3bn to ‌Ukraine to buy missiles and drones , Ursula von ⁠der ⁠Leyen, the European Commission president, ​has announced. Tusk said Russia was not ready for any peace talks “without the total capitulation of Ukraine”. “They are convinced the winter will be tragically critical for Ukraine.” He said last winter Poland stepped in with deliveries when Ukraine’s energy infrastructure came under attack, but if border crossings are destroyed it will be much harder for Warsaw to offer such help this winter. “Russia’s goal is to destroy as much as possible the economy and logistics of Ukraine,” Tusk said, adding that intelligence indicates continuous attacks of “very high frequency and intensity” on six main Ukrainian cities should be expected in the near future. A drone hit a petrol station near Ukraine’s border with Poland on Thursday, Tusk said separately at a press conference in Warsaw. A spokesperson for the Polish military told TVN24 that air defences were activated on Thursday after a jet-powered drone approached Polish airspace before exploding about 4km (2.5 miles) from the Polish border. Poland’s Lublin and Rzeszow ‌airports temporarily suspended operations on Thursday as the air force responded to Russian drone activity, Polish authorities said. Russian missiles and drones injured at least 19 people in Ukraine’s capital and the surrounding region , authorities said on Thursday. Kyiv’s military administration said more than 10 locations were hit, while 33 sites were damaged in the wider region. A 10-year-old girl and a 12-year-old boy were among the injured, the administration said. Ukraine’s air force said it destroyed or suppressed 131 Russian aerial targets during the overnight attack in the Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa regions. The attack involved ballistic and cruise missiles as well as drones and decoys. In Odesa, seven people were injured, including two children, according to Ukraine’s state emergency Service. Apartments on the 14th through 16th floors of a residential building were damaged. A private residential building in Odesa was also destroyed and others damaged. Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery in Yaroslavl and a military airfield in the Rostov region, Zelenskyy said on Thursday. Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s operation against the Yaroslavl oil refinery was conducted jointly by the country’s Security Service, special operations forces, military intelligence and the foreign intelligence service. The security service also struck a military airfield in Rostov, damaging an An-12 aircraft, two An-26s and three helicopters . Reuters said that according to its industry sources, the refinery halted crude processing after the Ukrainian ⁠attack. The local Russian governor confirmed the damage. A Russian drone struck a civilian vessel flying the flag of Tanzania in the Black Sea on Thursday, killing the ship’s captain and injuring three crew members , according to Oleh Kiper, the regional head in Odesa. Russia damaged the Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi bridge in the Odesa region, ⁠significantly limiting Ukraine’s ability to transport grain to its Danube river ports , Ukrainian state railway ⁠operator Ukrzaliznytsia ⁠said ​on Thursday. According to Ukrzaliznytsia, about 3,000 grain wagons ‌are bound for the Danube ports. Without the bridge, they would need ​26 days to reach the ports. “The situation is very difficult. We are working to restore the Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi bridge,” a company official said. https://www.abc57.com/news/man-who-fired.text: Man who fired at Goshen 7-Eleven same man who shot at ISP trooper in La Porte County, per police GOSHEN, Ind. -- Police are now identifying the man who allegedly shot at an Indiana State Trooper as the same who allegedly shot into a Goshen 7-Eleven. According to the Goshen Police Department, 22-year-old Jonathan Ybarra of Warsaw was the one who pulled up to the convenience store and fired shots at the building on September 18. No one was hurt in this incident. Following this, investigators say they used license plate reader information to locate the suspected vehicle in La Porte County. According to Indiana State Police, a trooper was flagged down by someone reporting two suspicious people walking on C.R. 125 E, south of C.R. 900 N. Investigators say the trooper found the pair, a man and a woman, and spoke with them. Officials say that when the trooper asked them for identification, Ybarra allegedly pulled out a gun and fired. The trooper was not injured; his patrol car was hit two times. The two ran into a wooded area. The woman suspect later surrendered. Ybarra was found a few hours later in a home at 8325 N. 125 E. Investigators say he was dead, with what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head. Goshen police say they are working with ISP on this investigation.
